title: Deliver the largest visible element within the documented threshold
statement: For the routes that receive most traffic, the element that occupies the largest area of the initial viewport finishes rendering within the threshold the metric definition publishes as good, measured at the seventy-fifth percentile of real visits.
rationale: That element is what a reader waits for before the page looks usable, so its timing is the closest available proxy for how long the page appears to take, and it is measured against a published threshold rather than a local opinion.
implementation: Identify the element per template rather than site-wide, then remove what delays it: a late-discovered image source, a font that blocks text, a data fetch on the critical path. Measure before and after on the same route, because a change that helps one template can harm another.

verification.method: Record the metric for each significant template from field data at the seventy-fifth percentile, and reproduce it in a lab run on a throttled connection.

caution: Meeting the threshold is not a ranking promise. The cited page-experience documentation describes these measurements as one input among many and states that great page experience does not override having relevant content, so no ranking outcome is claimed here.

sources.title: Understanding page experience in Google Search results

title: Prevent avoidable layout shift after first paint
statement: Content already visible does not move because a later-arriving image, advertisement, embed, font, or injected banner takes space that was not reserved for it.
rationale: A shift moves what the reader is currently looking at or about to tap, so the cost falls on the reader at the exact moment they were engaging with the page.
implementation: Reserve space for every element whose size is known only after it loads, including slots filled by third parties, and insert notices above the fold at render time rather than after. Declaring image dimensions removes the most common cause.

verification.method: Record the shift metric per template from field data and reproduce the largest contributing element in a lab run.

caution: This measurement is documented as part of page experience and is not a standalone ranking control. Improving it makes the page steadier to read, which is the outcome this record claims.

title: Keep the page responsive to input during load
statement: Interactions performed while the page is still loading are acknowledged within the threshold the interaction metric publishes as good, rather than queued behind long tasks on the main thread.
rationale: A reader who taps and sees nothing happen assumes the page is broken and taps again, so unresponsive load time produces both a worse experience and duplicated actions the application must handle.
implementation: Break long tasks so the main thread yields between units of work, defer non-essential script until after the first interaction is possible, and move heavy computation off the main thread. Hydrating less markup at once addresses the common case in a client-rendered application.

verification.method: Record the interaction metric from field data and attribute the worst cases to specific long tasks in a lab profile.

caution: As with the other measurements in this domain, the documented relationship to search is through page experience signals rather than a direct ranking rule, and no ranking effect is asserted.

title: Reduce time to the first byte of the document
statement: The document response begins arriving quickly enough that it does not dominate the time to first paint, and the site knows what that figure is for its own significant routes rather than for its home page alone.
rationale: Every later timing is offset by this one, so a slow first byte places a floor under the whole page that no client-side optimisation can lift.
implementation: Find whether the delay is in connection setup, in origin work, or in a blocking upstream call, and address the one that dominates. Serving a cached or prerendered document removes origin work from the path entirely where the content permits it.

verification.method: Measure the interval from request start to first byte for each significant route, separating connection setup from server processing.

caution: This is a diagnostic measurement rather than one of the metrics documented as a page-experience input, so it is included for the effect it has on the metrics that are.

title: Limit resources that block the first render
statement: Stylesheets and scripts in the document head that the first render does not need are deferred, made asynchronous, or moved, so the number of round trips before anything appears stays small.
rationale: Each blocking resource in the head postpones the entire first paint, which means a script unrelated to the visible content can delay every part of the page that is.
implementation: List what the head loads and classify each entry as needed for first render or not, then defer everything in the second group. Inlining only the styles the first viewport uses is the usual remedy for a large stylesheet.

verification.method: Capture the request waterfall for each significant route and identify resources fetched before first paint that the first viewport did not use.

caution: Deferring a stylesheet the first viewport does need trades one problem for a visible flash of unstyled content, so this control requires per-template measurement rather than a blanket change.

sources.title: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), resource load delay

title: Bound the cost of third-party scripts
statement: Each third-party script the site loads is accounted for by name, purpose, and measured cost, loads without blocking the first render, and is removed when nothing depends on it any more.
rationale: Third-party code runs on the site's pages with the site's performance consequences but outside its release process, so an upstream change alters the reader's experience without any deployment having happened.
implementation: Keep the inventory next to the loader configuration so adding a script requires recording its purpose, then load each entry asynchronously and measure its main-thread cost. Removing an unused tag is usually the largest available improvement.

verification.method: Attribute main-thread time and transferred bytes per origin in a lab profile and compare the result against the declared inventory.

caution: No published guidance sets a limit on third-party script cost, so this record is tier B. It asserts that the cost should be known and bounded by the site, not that any particular budget is correct.
